title: TOP 10 Most imported products from China to US (2026)
summary: What does the US import from China? Compare the top 10 product categories, 2025 values, the 2026 trade trend and the tariff checks to make before importing.
body_markdown:
Photo:[T Y / Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/cargo-ship-docked-at-a-busy-port-at-night-qDA8lNtL_90) .


**So,** **what does the US import from China** **? The top 10 imports in 2025 were cell phones and other household goods ($39.3 billion), electric apparatus ($21.5 billion), toys, games and sporting goods ($19.4 billion), apparel and textiles ($14.0 billion), other vehicle parts ($11.7 billion), computer accessories ($11.6 billion), other industrial machines ($10.7 billion), household appliances ($10.4 billion), telecommunications equipment ($10.0 billion) and computers ($9.7 billion), according to**[US Census Bureau end-use data](https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/statistics/product/enduse/imports/enduse_imports.xlsx) **.**


**In total,** **US imports from China** **fell to $308.7 billion in 2025, down 29.9% from $440.3 billion in 2024, per Census**[trade data for China](https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/balance/c5700.html) **. China slipped to the third-largest source of US goods imports, behind Mexico and Canada, with a 9.0% share. Annual rankings below are 2025 data, the latest full year.**

### **Cell phones lead, but far below 2024**


The Census category combines cell phones with other household goods not elsewhere classified. Its $39.3 billion total should therefore not be presented as a smartphone-only figure. It remains the largest category in this ranking, despite the 39.1% fall from 2024.


### **Computers posted the steepest drop**


Computers fell 71.7%, from $34.3 billion to $9.7 billion, the largest percentage decline among the top 10 categories. These are dollar values: they do not, by themselves, establish how much unit volumes changed or why sourcing shifted.


### Toys and apparel remain large categories


Toys, games and sporting goods fell 37.1% to $19.4 billion. The specific apparel category in the table fell 31.3% to $14.0 billion. That apparel category does not cover every type of clothing imported from China. Keep the classification consistent when comparing vendors or markets.


### **Machines and parts fell less**


**Industrial machines and vehicle parts fell less than most consumer categories. Other industrial machines slipped only 4.5% to $10.7 billion, the smallest decline in the top 10. Other vehicle parts and accessories fell 24.3% to $11.7 billion, household appliances fell 29.9% to $10.4 billion and telecommunications equipment fell 22.1% to $10.0 billion. Our analysis: factory equipment and replacement parts can be harder to re-source quickly than finished electronics, because buyers need to qualify a new vendor, but the data alone don't confirm that.**


**If you are researching** **what does the US import from China** **for your own category, the end-use table is a starting point; the HTS-level data in the tools section below gets you to your exact product.**


## **How US Imports From China Changed, 2016 to 2025**


**China was the largest source of US goods imports for years. Within the 2016–2025 period shown, its share peaked at 21.6% in 2017 and fell to 9.0% in 2025, as the chart shows. Mexico stayed the top source at $534.3 billion, up 6.2%, with Canada second at $381.9 billion. Meanwhile, imports from Vietnam rose 42.2% in 2025 to $193.9 billion and imports from Taiwan rose 73.2% to $201.4 billion. That pattern is consistent with sourcing moving away from China, but dollar values don't show volumes or the reasons behind each shift.**


**So** **what do we import from China** **now? Mostly finished consumer goods, electronics and parts, with a lower total dollar value than a decade ago.**


## **What US Imports From China Look Like in 2026**


**The decline continued into 2026.** **US imports from China** **were $215.0 billion from January through September 2026, down 11.5% from $242.9 billion a year earlier, according to the Census Bureau's**[September 2026 trade release](https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/Press-Release/current_press_release/index.html) **. September alone was higher than a year earlier, at $31.5 billion versus $23.5 billion, so watch the fourth quarter before calling a trend.**


**For importers, what you pay depends less on the totals and more on which tariffs apply to your specific product, which the next section covers.**

## **Does the US Import Food From China?**


**Yes, but it is a small share. US agricultural imports from China were $4.873 billion in fiscal year 2025, about 2.2% of all US agricultural imports, according to**[USDA's August 2026 trade outlook](https://www.ers.usda.gov/media/29488/aes-137.pdf) **. In that August outlook, USDA forecast $4.2 billion for fiscal 2026. This is a dated forecast, not a final fiscal-year result.**


## **What This Means for US Importers**


**For businesses that still buy from China, three practical points stand out. First, landed cost now depends heavily on your product's tariff layers, so two items in the same category can carry very different duties. Second, the 178 Section 301 exclusions are scheduled to end on January 9, 2027, so check whether your products are covered and plan for the possible change. Third, low-value shipments no longer enter duty-free, which affects ecommerce sellers that shipped small parcels directly from China.**


**Some importers are adding vendors in Vietnam, Taiwan, Mexico or India to spread risk, while others stay with established Chinese vendors because of cost, quality or capacity. Either way, it helps to price each order with the full duty in mind and to plan for the cash you pay before goods arrive.**

The**[Harmonized Tariff Schedule](https://hts.usitc.gov/) **gives base duty rates, and our**[China tariff page](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/tariff/china) **stacks the current layers for a product. **Knowing** **what does the US import from China** **in your category helps you price orders, plan inventory and see where competitors are shifting sourcing.**

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What does the US import from China the most?**


**By Census end-use category, the largest US import from China in 2025 was cell phones and other household goods, at $39.3 billion. Electric apparatus ($21.5 billion) and toys, games and sporting goods ($19.4 billion) came next. Together, the top 10 categories made up 51.3% of the $308.7 billion the US imported from China.**


### **What are the top 5 imports from China?**


**In 2025, the top five were cell phones and other household goods ($39.3 billion), electric apparatus ($21.5 billion), toys, games and sporting goods ($19.4 billion), apparel and textiles ($14.0 billion), and other vehicle parts and accessories ($11.7 billion), according to US Census Bureau end-use data. All five fell compared with 2024.**


### **How much does the US import from China?**


**The US imported $308.7 billion of goods from China in 2025, down 29.9% from $440.3 billion in 2024. From January through September 2026, imports were $215.0 billion, down 11.5% from the same period of 2025. China was the third-largest source of US imports in 2025, behind Mexico and Canada.**


### **Is China still the biggest US trading partner?**


**China was the third-largest source of US goods imports in 2025. It supplied 9.0% of US goods imports and ranked third, behind Mexico ($534.3 billion) and Canada ($381.9 billion), based on Census end-use data. China's share peaked at 21.6% in 2017. Taiwan ($201.4 billion) and Vietnam ($193.9 billion) ranked fourth and fifth in 2025, after imports from both rose sharply.**


### **What tariffs apply to Chinese imports in 2026?**


**As of November 12, 2026, many Chinese goods face Section 301 tariffs of 7.5% or 25% depending on the list (some major items, such as smartphones and laptops, are not on these lists), higher rates on products such as EVs and semiconductors, an additional 12.5% Section 301 duty since July 24, 2026, and Section 232 duties on covered metals. IEEPA tariffs were struck down in February 2026.**


### **Does the US import food from China?**


**Yes. US agricultural imports from China were about $4.9 billion in fiscal year 2025, roughly 2.2% of all US agricultural imports, according to USDA. USDA expects that figure to fall to about $4.2 billion in fiscal year 2026, so China remains a minor source of food for the US.**


### **Can I still import from China duty-free under $800?**


The duty-free de minimis exemption for ordinary commercial shipments remains suspended. CBP also established an informal-entry process for qualifying international mail in 2026. Check the applicable entry process and duties with your broker; a value below $800 does not establish duty-free eligibility.[CBP international-mail guidance](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/41fa7f0) .
